# Chapter 9: Common Design Patterns — 9.9–9.11

Rules that no analyzer enforces (judgment), and CONSIDER rules that analyzers only suggest. Open the examples file for the explanation and code the book gives with each rule.

## 9.9 Template Method

- **FDG9124** AVOID making public members virtual. — examples: examples/ch09-patterns-template-timeouts-xaml.md#fdg9124
- **FDG9125** CONSIDER using the Template Method Pattern to provide more controlled extensibility. — examples: examples/ch09-patterns-template-timeouts-xaml.md#fdg9125
- **FDG9126** CONSIDER naming protected virtual members that provide extensibility points for nonvirtual members by suffixing the nonvirtual member name with “Core.” — examples: examples/ch09-patterns-template-timeouts-xaml.md#fdg9126
- **FDG9127** DO perform argument and state validation in the nonvirtual member of the Template Method Pattern before calling the virtual member.
- **FDG9128** DO only perform argument and state validation unique to the derived type in the virtual member of the Template Method Pattern. That is, do not repeat validation from the nonvirtual member. — examples: examples/ch09-patterns-template-timeouts-xaml.md#fdg9128

## 9.10 Timeouts

- **FDG9129** DO prefer method parameters as the mechanism for users to provide timeout time. — examples: examples/ch09-patterns-template-timeouts-xaml.md#fdg9129
- **FDG9130** DO prefer using `TimeSpan` to represent timeout time. — examples: examples/ch09-patterns-template-timeouts-xaml.md#fdg9130
- **FDG9131** DO throw `System.TimeoutException` when a timeout elapses. — examples: examples/ch09-patterns-template-timeouts-xaml.md#fdg9131
- **FDG9132** DO NOT return error codes to indicate timeout expiration. — examples: examples/ch09-patterns-template-timeouts-xaml.md#fdg9132

## 9.11 XAML Readable Types

- **FDG9133** CONSIDER providing the default constructor if you want a type to work with XAML. — examples: examples/ch09-patterns-template-timeouts-xaml.md#fdg9133
- **FDG9134** DO provide markup extension if you want an immutable type to work with XAML readers. — examples: examples/ch09-patterns-template-timeouts-xaml.md#fdg9134
- **FDG9135** AVOID defining new type converters unless the conversion is natural and intuitive. In general, limit type converter usage to the ones already provided by .NET. — examples: examples/ch09-patterns-template-timeouts-xaml.md#fdg9135
- **FDG9136** CONSIDER applying the `ContentPropertyAttribute` to enable convenient XAML syntax for the most commonly used property. — examples: examples/ch09-patterns-template-timeouts-xaml.md#fdg9136
